title: Preparing My People: the band, principals and the three-week run
summary: Jones recalls the all-star second band, dancers and singers assembled in two days, and the show that caught on by word of mouth.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: How long did you work with the Chicago cast and band before they opened?
Well, it was just a couple of days at the most.

Because we had -- well, he got guys like Louis Bellson and Joey Benjamin and Bill Berry and -- who else? On the plane Duke says, "I'm going to give you Russell Procope and I'll go and get Hilton Jefferson for the road band."
Oh, I had a great band, you know?
John Sanders, Bootie Wood. All these

And he knew that I knew. By this time he knew, you know, that I knew, and was interested in it, that's the main thing. So some very funny things happened. He would never give me a conductor's sheet. I would ask for a conductor's sheet, he would walk away. And Strayhorn was like a little monster. He said, "Don't let him get away with that."
That's why Duke called him Little Monster, right?

Yeah. He'd say, "Don't let him get away with that. Get what you need." And then Duke told me -- of course we had the Alvin Ailey Dancers, the Talley Beatty Dancers, and Irving Bunton Choir, and a big orchestra, you know. And of course our principals, Lil Greenwood, Joya Sherrill, and Buddy Briggs. Let's see, who else? I can't think of anybody. Well, it was quite a -- I think it was 196 --
Yeah. So it's a -- I can't remember everybody now, at this point. But it was -- it was a fantastic show. Ill advertised, and it just caught on by word of mouth.
How long did it run in Chicago?
Three weeks. It was only booked for three weeks.
